thread:
incidents-bot: ALERT: hosted-runtime: KV-shard memory spike -> OOM risk on pool-hosts-03..05. metric: kv_shard_bytes_total > 95% for 3m. paging to #incidents

Jordan (oncall): I'm on it. seeing OOM traces from the runtime logs. impact: ~12% of hosted requests returning 5xx (OOM) over last 6m.

Maria (runtime): Confirmed. Looks like a single customer flow is producing extremely wide context that triggers per-shard slab allocations. Continuous-batching is amplifying the KV allocations.

Eli (sre): Can we throttle prefetch or reduce batching window as immediate mitigation?

Sasha (eng-runtime): Yes. Priority mitigations: 1) disable continuous-batching on hosted pool via feature-flag, 2) set kv_shard_max_prefetch=1 for now, 3) enable per-session slab caps. I can push a config change to the control plane.

Jordan (oncall): Execute steps 1 and 2 now. annotate with incident ID: INC-3700. I'll coordinate customer comms.

Sasha (eng-runtime): Pushing flag:
```
PATCH /runtime-configs/hosted-pool-03
{"continuous_batching_enabled": false, "kv_shard_max_prefetch": 1}
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for runtime-configs/hosted-pool-03 (rollout batch=3)

Jordan (oncall): Observing immediate drop in kv_shard_bytes_total on hosts-03..05. 5xx rate starting to decline (from 12% -> 4% in 90s).

Anna (cust-success): Any customers impacted badly? I have a ticket from ACME with multiple failed requests. Need ETA for fix before I escalate.

Eli (sre): Quick triage on ACME: the failing requests mapped to a single user session using huge prompt composition (history + embeddings + instructions). We'll classify as partial outage for that user flow.

Ryan (prod-eng): Do we have safe rollback plan if the config change causes regressions?

Sasha (eng-runtime): Yes. Rollback is just flip flag back on. But continuous-batching off increases p50 latency for small requests slightly (~10-30ms). We'll canary the change across 3 hosts first.

Jordan (oncall): Can we apply host-level prefetch cap to only affected tenants instead of global?

Sasha (eng-runtime): We can scope by tenant id, but need a quick mapping from request->tenant at control plane. ETA ~20m. For immediate safety we'll do global small blast to minimize risk.

Maria (runtime): Adding runtime-level guard to abort extremely long prefix KV growth: patching slab evict heuristic to run an early reclaim when per-shard growth > 200MB/s for >2 iterations.

Sasha (eng-runtime): Pushing slab-evict patch to canary hosts:
```
git rev: 9a7b1c2
apply: slab_eviction.early_reclaim=true
```

deploy-bot: canary deploy to hosted-pool-03a started

Jordan (oncall): Monitoring. New patch seems to keep memory stable on canary. No new OOMs reported. 5xx for ACME started to drop to 1.5%.

Anna (cust-success): I'll send a short note to the ACME account: "We're investigating intermittent failures caused by unusually large prompts; mitigation in progress; ETA for full mitigation 1-2h." Any objections?

Ryan (prod-eng): Good. Also we should capture a replayable example to add to eval/regression tests.

Eli (sre): Captured the offending session sample and saved to the RCA bucket: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/3700000000/ACME-session-3700.log

Maria (runtime): Follow-up root cause hypothesis: long prompt -> massive prefix KV insertion + continuous-batching combining multiple requests into shared batch -> per-shard slab growth beyond eviction speed -> OOM. Two points of amplification: continuous-batching and prefetch heuristics.

Jordan (oncall): Current status: continuous-batching off globally for hosted pool, kv_shard_max_prefetch=1 set. slab early-evict applied on canary and rolling to pool. Host OOM count back to baseline.

Sasha (eng-runtime): Next steps (short): 1) roll early-evict patch to remaining hosts (ETA 25m), 2) implement tenant-scoped prefetch cap (ETA 45m), 3) add permanent slab growth guard and alert (ETA 2d), 4) add regression test for large history sessions (ETA 3d).

Jordan (oncall): Assigning owners: Sasha -> rollout and permanent guard, Maria -> regression test and canary validation, Eli -> postmortem draft and alert tuning, Anna -> customer communications and post-incident notes.

Anna (cust-success): Sending update to ACME: "Mitigations deployed; you should see requests succeed now. We're still validating but will follow up in 2 hours with full writeup."

deploy-bot: rollout complete for runtime-configs/hosted-pool-03 (canary->pool).

Jordan (oncall): Confirming 5xx stabilized at 0.8% cluster-wide and memory metrics normalized. Marking incident as under control.

Sasha (eng-runtime): For completeness, we also toggled a temporary per-request KV ceiling: kv_request_max_bytes=200MB. That will prevent single requests from allocating unlimited slab. We'll revert to more nuanced throttling after further analysis.

Eli (sre): Will add alert: kv_shard_growth_rate > 150MB/min for 2m -> P1, and also add an internal test that simulates batching + large prefixes every deploy.

Maria (runtime): Note for postmortem: continuous-batching should include a budget guard that prevents combined-request growth beyond per-shard eviction capacity. We lacked signal there.

Jordan (oncall): Thanks all. I'll open INC-3700 in the tracker and tag owners. Postmortem draft requested in 48h.

Anna (cust-success): ACME replied: "Thanks, things look better. Please keep us posted."

Ryan (prod-eng): Follow-up action: we should consider making per-tenant prefetch caps default for hosted tier to limit blast radius. Putting a follow-up ticket in backlog.

Sasha (eng-runtime): Agreed. Also proposing a long-term improvement: KV sharding metrics per-tenant + adaptive prefetch based on eviction headroom.

Jordan (oncall): Closing slack handoff. Move to #postmortems when draft is ready. Good triage everyone. :tada:
